items.text: Carlos Queiroz resigned again as the head coach of Ghana's national football team three months after his return. The separation occurred by mutual agreement following recent defeats. Queiroz stated that ending the cooperation was the best decision for the future of Ghanaian football.

Iman Sadeghi, a 20-year-old blogger and detainee of the 1404 National Revolution in Kashan, has been sentenced to more than 13 years in prison. His charges include propaganda against the regime and publishing criminal content against national security. He was arrested on February 1, 2026, and transferred to Kashan prison.

A group of Iranians held an exhibition titled "The Corridor of Khamenei's Crimes" in Hanover, Germany. Similar exhibitions had previously been held in other European cities, including London. The exhibition focuses on the crimes of Khamenei.

Citizens have reported to Iran International about the high cost of dental care and their inability to pay for treatment. Some have had to extract teeth instead of repairing them due to high costs, while others have endured pain for months with painkillers and antibiotics. This issue was reported by Seba Heydarkhani.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in a meeting with entrepreneurs that the US should not expect to bring Iran to its knees through assassination. He added that the government is working to remove obstacles to exports and imports through land borders. He also emphasized that the Islamic Republic does not avoid dialogue and economic decisions must consider social tolerance.

Mostafa Dehpahlevan reported the involvement of some officials in illegal excavations and searches for historical artifacts. He mentioned that a member of parliament and a Friday prayer leader were present at these excavations. Mohsen Zahoori also pointed to the role of influential individuals and organized networks in the plundering of Iran's cultural heritage.

The Israeli Prime Minister praised the Indian pilot of the Flydubai flight for resisting an attacker and saving 174 passengers. Despite being seriously injured, the pilot opened the cabin door to allow passengers and crew to restrain the attacker. Netanyahu called him a true hero.

In Rasht, a young boy was attacked for wearing shorts. Educational expenses have risen sharply, and students are deprived of school books and supplies. It is also reported that police officers threaten students over taking food from restaurants.

The Israeli army announced that two commanders of the military wings of Hamas and Islamic Jihad were killed in airstrikes in Gaza and Jabalia. These individuals had entered Israeli territory during the October 7 attack and were involved in the abduction of six people. The Israeli army stated that the strikes were carried out to neutralize threats and respond to ceasefire violations.

Masoumeh Taherkhani said the current path of the dollar is not decreasing, but the Central Bank can slow its growth. She mentioned the possible injection of two billion dollars, restrictions on Tether transactions, and allocation of currency for essential imports. She considered these measures to have no significant effect on the market.

The IRGC and Iranian officials are holding training courses on weapon use for civilians in Iran. These trainings include how to use Kalashnikovs, sniper rifles, and RPGs. The purpose is to prepare for possible military conflicts and to preserve the regime's survival.
Alireza Abdoli won the gold medal in Greco-Roman wrestling at the Nagoya Asian Games. Mehdi Bali lost in the semifinals with a score of 5 to 4. Sajjad Abbaspour finished in fifth place.

Following the first round of student protests at Allameh Tabataba'i University, a video has been released showing students posting notices around the university announcing their intention to continue the protests.

On the twelfth day of the Asian Games in Nagoya, opponents of the Islamic Republic held a protest gathering. Some spectators faced confrontations with officials for carrying the Lion and Sun flag. The report was provided by Alireza Modiri from Iran International.

The head of Hamadan University of Medical Sciences announced that 100,000 phone harassment cases were recorded in the Hamadan emergency system in 1404. More than 400 harassing calls were registered from one line. A legal expert suggested increasing penalties for phone harassers and using supplementary punishments.

Farzaneh Fasihi, Iran's Olympic runner, called Ehsan Haddadi the most notorious athlete in Iran's history and said young athletes should take him as a lesson. This reaction came after Haddadi's remarks about female athletes, advising them to become virtual celebrities or champions. Fasihi also referred to Haddadi's legal case in the 2010s involving accusations of sexual assault.

The US President, in an interview with Time magazine, stated that he rejected the recent proposal by the Islamic Republic to end conflicts and reopen the Strait of Hormuz due to its "insufficiency." He added that he does not rule out the possibility of escalating US military attacks against the Islamic Republic. Trump also claimed to have destroyed Iran's nuclear capabilities, navy, air force, and radar.

The British ambassador in Tehran was summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs due to the UK Prime Minister's remarks about Iran's role in the incident at Fairford Air Base. The Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister rejected these statements and conveyed Tehran's protest. He also requested an official explanation from the UK government.
Reza Alipour won the silver medal in the speed climbing event at the Nagoya Asian Games with a time of 5.36 seconds.

The price of chicken and groceries has reached 30 million tomans. In Rasht, social tensions with the presence of security forces and aerial gunfire have been reported. Additionally, schools in Mazandaran are facing gas shortages and gas stations are crowded.

Iran's tennis team has won four medals in the history of the Asian Games. The last medals were two silvers at the 1974 Asian Games in Tehran. Taghi Akbari, Ali Madani, and Kambiz Derafshijavan won these medals.

Hossein Yekta, a commander of the IRGC, announced his presence by the Litani River in southern Lebanon. He stated that just as they performed ablution in the Tigris and prayed in Karbala, he is now performing ablution in front of Israeli eyes and will pray in Jerusalem. Yekta also added that everything Ali Khamenei said has come true.

At the end of the twelfth day of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Iran secured its twelfth medal and entered the top five teams in the standings. Alireza Abdoli won gold in the 77 kg Greco-Roman wrestling final, and Reza Alipour earned silver in speed climbing. Iran ranks fifth with 12 gold medals, tied with Thailand in golds but ahead due to more silver medals.

Associated Press reported, citing two American officials, that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio asked Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave New York early after indirect negotiations with the Islamic Republic failed to make progress.

Representatives of the new Syrian government and Hezbollah met secretly in Turkey to reduce security tensions. This is their first known direct meeting since the fall of Bashar al-Assad. Turkey played a role in organizing the meeting.

Russia has warned NATO that if it intervenes to cut off Kaliningrad's connection with Russian territory, Moscow is prepared to use all its military capabilities, including nuclear weapons. This warning was reported by Lily Nickfar from Iran International.

The Conservative Party of Canada has called for a reduction in immigration following Mark Carney's remarks about a possible increase in immigration. The party argues that housing, health, and employment infrastructure cannot support this level of immigration. More details were reported by Mahsa Mortazavi.

Rafael Leao will wear Cristiano Ronaldo's number 7 jersey in Portugal's match against Denmark in the UEFA Nations League. Ronaldo left the national team camp one day before the match. This decision was made by UEFA.

Donald Trump, in an interview with Time magazine, said there is a possibility of intensifying US airstrikes on Iran after the midterm elections. He also said that after attacking Iran's nuclear facilities, the US continued the strikes because it was concerned that Tehran would resume its nuclear activities elsewhere.

Donald Trump emphasized that resolving Iran's nuclear issue is a fundamental condition for any agreement. He did not rule out the possibility of resuming military attacks after the midterm elections. Trump stated that Iran will eventually be forced to accept the US nuclear conditions.

Branch 23 of Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Khosro Mohammadi-Nia, Masoud Tushmalani, and Sirvan Shabani to death. These three were arrested during the December 2025 protests and are held in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj. Their charges include waging war against God and acting in favor of hostile governments.

A citizen reported that over the past five days, several military vehicles carrying missile launchers have been stationed in central Sabzevar and around schools. Additionally, Basij and IRGC forces have been present in these areas. The report was accompanied by a video.

The Israeli army announced that after investigations, 170 Gaza residents who were identified as journalists and media activists were members of groups such as Hamas and Islamic Jihad. The army released images and documents showing these individuals' affiliations. Hamas and Islamic Jihad also identified some of these individuals as their members.

Taxi fares in Iran have risen up to half a million tomans. Power outages in Khorramabad continue daily for 1 to 3 hours. Additionally, high costs of education, healthcare, and equipment repairs have caused public concern.

French authorities reported the arrest of over 600 people and injury of 83 police officers during student protests. The student union stated that entrances to about 400 high schools have been blocked. These protests are expanding.

British counter-terrorism police arrested a dual British-Iranian citizen on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. The arrest took place near the RAF Fairford base. The British Prime Minister has accused Iran of involvement in the incident.

American forces withdrew from their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday, October 8, 2024. This withdrawal was based on an agreement made during Joe Biden's presidency. Iraqi officials and analysts have warned about the security implications of this move.

Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, posted a video on X about his speech at the UN General Assembly regarding China and Russia's veto of the expert panel monitoring sanctions on Iran. He said these sanctions were imposed due to Iran's illegal nuclear weapons pursuit. Waltz announced that the US will form its own expert panel and invited countries to join to ensure Iran never acquires nuclear weapons.

A video showing the drying of trees in Chitgar Park, Tehran, has been released. Some citizens attribute this to negligence in irrigation by the municipality. There are also claims of intentional tree drying for construction purposes.

The US Treasury Department added two individuals and 29 companies and entities related to Iran to its sanctions list on Thursday evening, October 8. Among the sanctioned Iranian entities are Iran Khodro, Iran Khodro Diesel, Saipa, Pars Khodro, Zamyad, Hepco, the Islamic Republic of Iran Railways, and Raja Passenger Trains Company. Companies in China, Hong Kong, the UAE, Turkey, Germany, and Indonesia were also added to the list.

Iran International reported that the Islamic Republic systematically uses violence against nationalist protesters. The violence includes direct shooting, threats of amputation, and burning or skinning due to nationalist tattoos. Tattoos such as Reza Shah Pahlavi's signature and the Lion and Sun symbol have led to violent confrontations.

The One Million Signatures campaign started in September 2006 aiming to change discriminatory laws against women. The campaign focused on direct dialogue and legal education, bringing the issue of legal discrimination against women into public discourse. The 20th anniversary of the campaign prompted an interview with Mansoureh Shojaei about the experience and legacy of this movement.

Donald Trump confirmed the possibility of the Islamic Republic's role in the Flydubai plane incident and said the matter is under investigation. He also warned that if Iran's involvement is proven, the US will respond strongly. Trump also made statements about Iran's nuclear program and negotiations with the Islamic Republic.

A birthday ceremony for Arzoo Abedi was held at her grave. This 50-year-old fitness coach and mountaineer was shot in Isfahan on the evening of January 8 and died. Her two children were with her at the time.

Donald Trump claimed that he eliminated Iran's nuclear threat in one night, which he had previously said would take 4 to 6 weeks. He added that the remaining time is just to ensure the situation stays the same.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, wrote on the social media platform X that the Iranian government's ability to finance its war machine and spread terror globally has significantly decreased thanks to "economic exclusion" operations. He added that today's action directly targets their supporters and paves the way for the US and its partners to cut off the Iranian government's revenues once and for all.

Megamotor company was hit by shrapnel during the 40-day war and damages such as broken windows have not yet been repaired. Employees' salaries, under the Saipa subsidiary, have been paid irregularly after the war. The workers are in a difficult situation and worried about supporting their families.

The program Geography of the National Revolution examines the nationwide protests of December 2025 and their suppression patterns. The next episode will focus on Zanjan province. Iran International has asked viewers to send information and images related to these protests.
A video shows a convoy of military forces and equipment moving in Abadan towards the Shalamcheh border crossing. This movement was reported on the 8th of Mehr. Local residents have confirmed this.

Rasoul Yousefi Azar, a citizen of Mahabad, was arrested on Tuesday to serve a six-month prison sentence and was transferred to Mahabad prison. This action was taken to enforce the judicial sentence. More information is available in the original text.

Rouhani spoke at a gathering of supporters of the Islamic Republic in Tehran. He said Mojtaba Khamenei, the absent leader of the regime, was present at the gathering for half an hour the night before. Until now, no audio or video of Mojtaba Khamenei had been seen.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur, reported that ethnic and religious minorities in Iran face various forms of discrimination including linguistic, economic restrictions, and deprivation from education and employment. She highlighted the impact of this discrimination on the criminal justice system and concerns about torture and violations of fair trial rights. Sato emphasized that death sentences related to minorities should be carefully reviewed.

A citizen reported buying a bottle of carbonated malt drink and a raw cocktail sausage for 115,000 tomans. He criticized the high prices and said he did not know whether to cry or laugh. This highlights the rising prices of basic goods in Iran.

A documentary titled "Spider House" about hackers of the Islamic Republic has been released. The documentary examines how the Islamic Republic identifies, employs, and uses hackers. It shows how hackers can become tools of a ruthless system.

Abbas Araghchi proposed during private meetings in New York that inspectors be allowed access to bombed nuclear facilities in exchange for sanctions relief. This proposal was made on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Araghchi also requested the cancellation of the UN sanctions reinstatement decision, which European officials have opposed so far.

Mahdi Abiyat, a 31-year-old citizen of Ahvaz, was arrested by Intelligence Department agents in Ahvaz. The arrest took place without a judicial warrant on a street in the Kooye Shahrak neighborhood of Ahvaz. Mahdi Abiyat was transferred to an unknown location.

After receiving documents from Real Madrid, UEFA reactivated the investigation into the Negreira case involving Barcelona. Real Madrid also issued a statement demanding swift action from UEFA. However, Barcelona stated that this is not a new case and it was never closed.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International complaining about the poor quality of the Tehran to Zahedan train. The train was stopped due to a repair of a malfunction. It eventually arrived at the destination with a six-hour delay.

UKMTO reported that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile while passing through the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire. The crew is reported to be safe. The extent of damage and environmental impact is not yet known.

Dalga Khatinoglu, an oil and energy expert, said crude oil exports of regional Arab countries, including Oman, in September were 500,000 barrels per day more than in the pre-war period and also increased significantly last week. He added that these countries have increased exports to the market using oil reserves and help from the US naval fleet. Khatinoglu also stated that Iran's oil loading and sales are currently halted and Tehran's return to the Chinese market will be difficult, even if an agreement is reached with the US.

Alireza Kiani critiques the view that equates constitutional monarchy with the rule of the jurisprudent in the thirteenth episode of the program 'Fereydoun.' The critique was presented in the thirteenth episode. The discussion focuses on the differences between these two systems.

The club Eldense announced that Lionel Messi has become the new owner. The Colombian investment group TH transferred its shares to Messi. This is Messi's first ownership of a professional club in Spain.

Miad Maleki stated that the new US sanctions mainly target supply, sales, and goods transfer networks in Iran's neighboring countries. Iranian companies in sectors like metals and automotive rely on networks in Turkey and the UAE. Regional countries' concerns about the Islamic Republic's activities have increased the likelihood of their cooperation in enforcing the sanctions.

Alireza Kiani explains in the program 'Fereydoun' why the Islamic Republic cannot be considered a rule of law. He states that the supremacy of the Supreme Leader's will over the law makes citizens' rights subject to the will of power.

Nabil Fahmi, Secretary-General of the Arab League, stated that Arab countries' relations with Iran are not shaped by US and Israeli calculations. He emphasized that Iran cannot impose anything on the region and stability requires good neighborliness. Fahmi also told Abbas Araghchi that aggression against any Arab land is unacceptable.

Alireza Kiani discusses the authority of the Pahlavi kings and the reduction of the king's executive role in the program 'Fereydoun.' He refers to Britain's experience of maintaining the monarchy alongside changes in its powers. This topic was covered in the thirteenth episode of the program.

After Portugal's match against Denmark, Jorge Jesus avoided answering questions about his conflict with Cristiano Ronaldo and emphasized focusing on the next game against Norway. He stated that the rules are the same for everyone and that focusing is not difficult for him. Jesus promised to discuss the issue after the match with Norway.

The U.S. Treasury Department announced that as part of efforts to block Iran's sanctions evasion routes, it has sanctioned a number of companies and intermediaries in China, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, Indonesia, and Germany.

Shayan Samiei stated that the new US sanctions target the automotive, railway, and related networks of the Islamic Republic. These sanctions increase pressure on income, production, and sanction evasion routes. Additionally, companies in Germany, Turkey, and the UAE are included in this sanction package.

Four years have passed since the Bloody Friday of Zahedan, when people went out for prayer and justice and were met with gunfire. The UN fact-finding team reported 103 deaths that day. The pursuit of justice by the families of the victims and the wounded continues.

Mohammad Mashinchian stated that managing the country and continuing the operation of major industries is not possible under current conditions. These remarks were made in a program on Iran International TV. The full episode is available on YouTube.

46 countries at the UN Human Rights Council condemned the increased use of the death penalty by the Islamic Republic. They expressed concern about the execution of protesters and violations of due process rights. The statement was read by the representative of Liechtenstein.

Bert Eriksson stated that the US, after pressuring Iran at sea and air, is now restricting Iran's economic lifelines on land. These restrictions have put pressure on people's livelihoods. Iran's economy is facing high inflation and a declining rial value.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran did not load any crude oil onto tankers in September. He attributed this to the pressure campaign by the Trump administration to cut off the Islamic Republic's main source of revenue. The US Treasury also announced that it had launched an economic exclusion operation to cut off Iran's financial resources.

Donald Trump said the war with the Islamic Republic will end very soon and Tehran must make the right decision. He added that the US has almost complete control of the Strait of Hormuz and the Islamic Republic faces 312% inflation and currency collapse. Trump also said Washington is still trying to negotiate and oil prices will drop sharply after the war.

EU ministers met in Luxembourg to discuss migration, security, and the Schengen area. The main focus was on returning asylum seekers without residence permits. Strengthening cooperation with non-EU countries to repatriate their nationals was also a key topic.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, stated that the Islamic Republic has violated laws and refuses to abandon its nuclear ambitions. He referred to the IAEA's recent referral of Iran's case to the Security Council. Waltz also accused Russia and China of blocking UN sanctions against Iran.

Donald Trump said it appears that the Islamic Republic was involved in the incident at the Royal Air Force base in Fairford, but he cannot confirm this with certainty. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic's efforts will soon end and their army has been defeated. Trump also stated that their navy and air force have been destroyed.

Donald Trump said the Islamic Republic was only weeks away from obtaining nuclear weapons and the US had no choice but to act. He described the leaders of the Islamic Republic as "crazy" and emphasized that the US has almost full control over the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also stated that the war will end soon and the Islamic Republic must make a smart decision.

Ashton Hamid Al-Aboudi, an employee of the US Department of Energy, was arrested for attempting to provide material support to Yemen's Houthis. He is accused of procuring drone parts and chemicals and offering technical advice to the Houthis. The charges are unproven, and if convicted, he could face up to 20 years in prison.

Iran is entering winter with chronic gas shortages and reduced production capacity. The First Vice President stated that 250 million cubic meters of gas were lost from the network during two recent wars, and the government hopes to restore 100 million cubic meters. Gas shortages may lead to reduced production, power outages, and increased pollution.

The US has deployed two Patriot missile defense batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar in recent weeks. This move aims to protect the oil and gas facilities of these countries in case of renewed military operations against Iran. It was done at the request of Saudi and Qatari leaders to reassure them.

A Russian government internal document shows that 68% of its trade with Iran is conducted in rubles and rials. This is while Vladimir Putin had announced in January 2025 that the figure was 95%. Russia has even set a target of 71% for 2026.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic was only three to four weeks or less away from acquiring nuclear weapons. He said Iran has not been able to pass a ship through the Strait of Hormuz for months and the US is removing millions of barrels of oil from the region. Trump predicted the crisis will end soon and oil prices will drop.

Farhad Alavi stated that new US sanctions against Iran's automotive, railway, and heavy industries aim to reduce the Islamic Republic's revenue sources. These sanctions cut supply chains and limit foreign companies' cooperation. The main goal is to economically pressure and restrict the government's financial resources.

Aydin Panahi stated that the Islamic Republic did not export any crude oil in the first month of the war. The only remaining oil revenue is from oil that was already on water before the war. He also mentioned increasing pressure on Tehran's economy and foreign exchange resources as the gas and budget crisis approaches.

The UK permanent representative to the UN stated that UN sanctions related to Iran's nuclear program remain binding despite the veto on extending the expert mission's mandate. She added that ending this mission will make monitoring sanctions more difficult. She also emphasized that Iran has accumulated over 400 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60 percent.

Priest Vartan Avanesian stated that pressure on Christians in Iran began in the early years of the Islamic Republic. He said Christians are still imprisoned due to their religious beliefs. Although human rights organizations for Christians are active, much work remains to bring their voices to the global community.

A SpaceX spacecraft carrying four astronauts was launched from Florida and docked with the International Space Station in the fastest American crewed spacecraft trip, taking 7 hours and 55 minutes. Jessica Watkins commands the mission and is the first Black woman to lead this group. The astronauts include two Americans, one Canadian, and one Russian, and they will conduct research focused on human health and performance in orbit.

Pakistan's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the attack by Iran-backed Houthis on the Taybah power distribution station in Medina. The attack on the civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Prophet's Mosque was described as provocative. Pakistan reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its efforts for peace in the region.

China announced that it vetoed the resolution related to the sanctions experts panel on the Islamic Republic. It considers the activation of the snapback mechanism and the reinstatement of sanctions legally and procedurally flawed. China believes these actions harm diplomatic efforts to resolve the nuclear issue.

Pouria Taherkhani lost 5-2 to Kim Hidong of South Korea in the bronze medal match of the under 94 kg jujitsu category at the Nagoya Asian Games, missing out on a bronze medal. He had reached the semifinals with three victories. After losing in the semifinals, Taherkhani was also defeated in the bronze medal match.

Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said at a ceremony in Neka that the survival of Mojtaba Khamenei during the US and Israeli attack is definitely a miracle. He added that Mojtaba Khamenei studied and taught in Qom and Tehran. Nikzad described this as a sign of a miracle.

Rouhollah Rahimipour, journalist and political analyst, referring to Donald Trump's remarks, said these statements do not necessarily indicate a final decision, but Washington is moving toward adopting one. He described Trump's warnings as serious and real and said the Islamic Republic faces a binary choice between an agreement or submitting to a highly destructive and exhausting war.

The company Troi Trading based in Istanbul has been included in the latest US sanctions. The US Treasury announced that this company sent truck parts to Bahman Diesel. Bahman Diesel is a subsidiary of the Bahman Group.

Iran International has reported that an Israeli infiltrator spy, a graduate of Imam Sadegh University, enabled key Mossad operations in Iran by exploiting security gaps. These operations include sabotage at the Natanz nuclear facility and an explosion at the Malard missile center. These exclusive documents and information were published by Iran International.

Alireza Mostafaei, a disabled protester, announced that his Instagram page was blocked due to his support for political prisoners and Reza Pahlavi. He has been summoned by the judiciary on charges of propaganda against the regime. A case has been filed against him.

Pakistan's Foreign Ministry announced that Islamabad adheres to all applicable sanctions against the Islamic Republic of Iran. This comes despite Pakistan previously opposing unilateral sanctions against Iran. The report was provided by Javad Hamdani from Iran International.

Iman Aghayari, a political analyst, referred to the joint statement of 46 countries at the UN Human Rights Council. These statements are important for documenting human rights violations and protesting executions. The Islamic Republic accepts the least impact from global protests.

Attacks on bridges in the war with the Islamic Republic have become a more prominent tactic. These attacks are significant due to the location of bridges near rail networks, main roads, and military bases. This highlights logistical vulnerabilities.

The advisor to the head of the Welfare Organization announced a shortage of capacity in elderly care centers. At least 600,000 elderly people need care, but only about 20,000 receive services at home. Urban environments and public transportation are also not suitable for the needs of the elderly.

A video shows Bahram Yousefi's son blowing out his father's birthday candle. Bahram Yousefi, who owned a children's clothing production unit in Tehran's market, was killed by officers on January 8, 2026, in the Naziabad neighborhood. This incident has been reflected on social media.

Ali Farhadi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Education, denied reports of teachers' resignations. He stated that this issue is not true and is a rumor. He also mentioned that with the reopening of schools for in-person education, teachers and students have welcomed the return to classroom learning.

Morteza Dehghan, Deputy Minister of Roads and Urban Development, stated that Iran's airspace is open unlike the US. Iran exchanges air traffic with 12 neighboring countries and flights operate according to international regulations. Flight safety is fully ensured and all flights are serviced.

Akbar Hasanpour's wife released a video showing moments from his birthday and funeral. Akbar Hasanpour was killed on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Gohardasht, Karaj by government forces. The video was published on the occasion of his birthday.
Donald Trump posted images on Truth Social showing protesters marching in Isfahan. The images are from December. Trump published these images on Thursday, September 30.

Hadi Ahmadi, spokesperson for the Iranian Pharmacists Association, reported a liquidity crisis in the drug supply chain. He stated that delays in payment have caused over 8 billion rials worth of pharmacy checks to bounce. Ahmadi warned that this situation could lead to drug shortages and reduced access for the public.

Alex Ferguson was afraid to return to Old Trafford after emergency brain surgery in 2018. He did not know how fans would react but was met with strong applause. Ferguson also spoke about his recovery process and losing his voice during that time.

Abbas Mazloom died at the age of 41 after being hospitalized for 49 days following injuries sustained during protests. A video showing his last days in the hospital has been released. He was a father of two and is seen in a conversation with his mother.

Mohammad Nokhodi won the gold medal in the 86 kg freestyle wrestling category at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games by defeating Ishiguro Hayato 9-6 in the final. He had previously defeated Rabi Abu Aryaleh, Lee, and Malik Shaweif in earlier rounds. This gold medal is the 13th for the Iranian delegation at these games.

Masoud Shahdusti, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Hormoz, warned that if Arab countries attack Iran, neither the region nor Europe will be safe. He stated that if an attack comes from the land or air of regional countries, Iran will not show restraint and will deliver a severe and decisive blow.

Amirhossein Zare won the gold medal in the 125 kg freestyle wrestling final at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games by defeating Bohrdon from China 14-2. He had also defeated his previous opponents with decisive results. This victory marked Iran's 14th gold medal in the Games.

Ata Hosseinian stated that gas shortage in Iran has reached 300 to 400 million cubic meters per day. In case of a cold winter, gas supply to households and industries in the northern half of the country may be cut off. This could lead to increased mazut burning, air pollution, and widespread power outages.

Saghar Moradi won the gold medal in the 67-kg taekwondo final at the Asian Games by defeating the Uzbek representative 2-0. She is the first Iranian female taekwondo athlete to win a gold medal in the history of the Asian Games. Moradi defeated her opponents in earlier rounds to reach the final.

Iranian authorities used oil company facilities to suppress protests in Khuzestan province. Medical staff were instructed to cooperate with security agencies to identify injured protesters. This information was reported by Iran International.

The Esteghlal football team faces travel restrictions for the second week of the Asian Elite League in Qatar, and club officials are awaiting a response from Qatar. Esteghlal has requested a direct flight to Qatar but has not yet received a reply. If a direct flight is not possible, Esteghlal has two travel options: from Tabriz to Istanbul and then to Qatar, or from Basra to Qatar.

The human rights website Hal Va Sh reported that at least five members of the Fatemiyoun Brigade were killed in an armed attack in the Rudmahi area of Zahedan. The attack involved a roadside bomb explosion and gunfire. The Quds Base of the IRGC also confirmed the death of one of its forces.

A viewer reported in a video that on October 2nd, they paid over half a million tomans for a bottle of soda and a bucket of yogurt. They sarcastically called the Islamic Republic the "number one superpower in the world." The video was sent to Iran International.

The UAE has declared the incident on the Flydubai flight as a terrorist act. The UAE Attorney General's office has started official interrogations of the co-pilot on charges of terrorism links. Israeli security officials have requested to have observers present during the interrogations.

The IRGC announced it is ready to respond immediately and more severely than Operation Promised Truth 2 to any threat or attack. This statement was issued on the second anniversary of the Islamic Republic's attacks on Israel. The IRGC emphasized that the era of cost-free threats has ended.

The Central Bank of the Islamic Republic announced it will use intervention tools to manage currency market fluctuations. The institution monitors currency market developments and will act if necessary to maintain monetary and currency stability. It will also take necessary measures to prevent non-fundamental trends in the market.

At least 140 people were arrested during protests in Bojnord between January 3 and 10, 2026. The number of detainees reached 180 by the end of January. Some of those arrested included a former judiciary employee and a nurse.
